78382.body:

Caption: 

“You're thinking of this place all wrong, as if I had the money back in a safe.”
_— George Bailey on fractional-reserve banking_



----------View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/ef7486a8-a41a-4a16-8509-8c69f9ace4a2/unnamed.jpg?t=1788297332)
Caption: 

# It's a wonderful bank

The fundamental promise of banking is that everyone can have their money back whenever they want it — as long as they don't all want it at the same time.

We learned that from George Bailey.

"You're thinking of this place all wrong, as if I had the money back in a safe,” he [told](https://youtu.be/EOzMdEwYmDU?si=BBTgiFtj_kTunqU7) the customers making a run on the Bailey Brothers Building & Loan. “The money's not here. Your money's in Joe's house, that's right next to yours. And in the Kennedy house, and Mrs. Macklin's house, and a hundred others.”

“_You’re_ lending them the money to build and then they’re going to pay it back to you as best they can," he explained.

The crowd of worried customers was not immediately reassured. George had to offer $2,000 of his own money to fend off the run. Even then, the bank wasn’t truly saved until the very end of the movie, when friends and customers donated enough money to cover an $8,000 hole in the bank’s balance sheet.

Austrian economist Murray Rothbard would have told them to let Bailey Bros. fail. “Fractional-reserve banking is a shell game, a Ponzi scheme, a fraud,” he once [wrote](https://mises.org/library/book/mystery-banking?d7_alias_migrate=1).

He believed banks were only able to perpetrate that fraud because bankers like George Bailey misrepresent how they were able to make so many loans.

“Because everybody's been inured to thinking that the banks simply borrow our money and re-lend it,” Rothbard [explained](https://freecapitalists.org/courses/economics-101/banking-and-the-business-cycle/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) in a lecture, “it's very difficult to make the mind shift and realize that the banks are really engaging in a form of legalized counterfeiting.”

In other words, if people understood how fractional-reserve banking _really_ worked — that the banks create money “out of thin air” — everyone would ask for their money back at the same time. Even the best banks would fail.

Caption: 

Welcome to the DefiLlama Newsletter. Each week we bring you the most valuable onchain insights from the the deepest DeFi dataset in the world.

_Gmail users: if this arrived in your Promotions folder, drag this email to your Primary folder._





## Pons Launchpad: a generational run

_“I’ve personally never seen anything like this where we go 0 to 100 in this short amount of time.” — Pons founder_

Tweet:  (https://twitter.com/FullyVested_Pod/status/2094604822439727289?s=20)

Pons is a non-custodial launchpad for fixed-supply tokens on Robinhood Chain.

DefiLlama’s tracked activity starts July 14th when Pons was pulling in ~$150k in daily fees.

A week later, daily fees had already crossed $1m. Yesterday, Pons brought in $4.89m in fees, a 31x increase in seven weeks.

## fomo: a social trading growth machine

fomo is a mobile-first trading app merging token swaps, social feeds, leaderboards and copy-trading.

The gasless app is crypto’s newest onboarding channel, adding 30,000 new users per day and hosting 1.2m monthly active users in August.

In the last 30 days fomo crossed $1.1b in both DEX and perp volume, more than double each metric MoM. Yesterday, fomo crossed $1m in daily fees for the first time.
